Is Your Home Cool But Still Sticky?

settings.editor: If your home feels cool but still sticky, the problem may be humidity, not the thermostat. High indoor humidity can make rooms feel warmer, create musty odors, leave basements or lower levels feeling damp, and make your AC work harder during humid Tri-Cities summers.

Air Comfort Services helps homeowners across the Tri-Cities understand what is causing humidity problems and what solutions make sense for their home. With 40+ years of combined HVAC experience, we explain what is happening, what your options are, and how humidity control can help your home feel fresher and more balanced.
No hidden fees. No pressure. Just clear answers and up-front pricing.

settings.title: Is It Time to Consider Humidity Control?

settings.editor: Not every humid room means you need new equipment. Sometimes the right fix is AC maintenance, airflow correction, ductwork evaluation, or thermostat adjustments. But if your home regularly feels damp, musty, or uncomfortable even when the AC is running, humidity control may be the right next step.

settings.title: You may want to consider humidity control if:

icon_list.text: Your home feels sticky even when the AC is on
Rooms feel cool but still uncomfortable
Your basement or lower level feels damp
Your AC runs often but comfort does not improve
You are concerned about mold or mildew conditions
Your home struggles during humid Northeast Tennessee afternoons

settings.editor: Proper humidity control can help your home feel cooler and more comfortable without constantly lowering the thermostat. It may also help reduce unnecessary AC strain by managing moisture more effectively.
We will not recommend equipment you do not need. If maintenance, airflow improvements, or another HVAC solution makes more sense, we will explain that option too.
The goal is simple: help you protect your comfort, your home, and your long-term peace of mind.

settings.title: Humidity Control Options for Tri-Cities Homes

settings.editor: Every home handles moisture differently. The right humidity control solution depends on your HVAC system, home layout, insulation, ventilation, basement conditions, and comfort concerns. We help homeowners understand which option fits their home best.

A whole-home dehumidifier works with your HVAC system to help remove excess moisture from the air throughout the home. This can be especially helpful in houses that feel damp during summer, have musty lower levels, or struggle with humidity even when the AC is running.

tabs.tab_title: How do I know if my home has too much humidity?
tabs.tab_content: Common signs include sticky air, musty odors, damp rooms, condensation on windows, allergy-like symptoms indoors, and a home that feels uncomfortable even when the AC is running. Musty odors are often connected to excess moisture, so they should not be ignored.

tabs.tab_title: What indoor humidity level is best?
tabs.tab_content: Many homes feel most comfortable when indoor humidity stays around 30% to 50%. The right range can depend on the season, home conditions, and comfort needs.
Yes, your AC removes some moisture as it cools. However, if the system is short cycling, oversized, dirty, or struggling with airflow, it may not remove enough humidity to keep your home comfortable.

tabs.tab_title: Is a whole-home dehumidifier better than a portable dehumidifier?
tabs.tab_content: A whole-home dehumidifier can manage moisture more broadly through the HVAC system, while portable units only treat specific rooms. The best option depends on your home, humidity levels, and comfort goals.

tabs.tab_title: Do I need humidity control if my home already has central AC?
tabs.tab_content: Possibly. Central AC can help with moisture, but some homes still struggle with humidity because of airflow issues, system sizing, ductwork, basement moisture, or long humid summers.
